results.title: Keiko Fujimori takes office as president of Peru with the promise of a ‘safe, prosperous, and united’ country | International | EL PAÍS English
results.author: Renzo Gómez Vega
highlights: Twenty-six years after Alberto Fujimori resigned via fax from Japan, as his government crumbled following the exposure of a widespread corruption scandal, Fujimorism has returned to power in Peru. His daughter, Keiko Fujimori, will be sworn in as president of the Republic on July 28, the day Peru commemorates its independence. At 51, she becomes the first woman elected by popular vote to lead the country. Her inauguration brings to a close a long journey marked by three failed presidential campaigns, but it also ushers in a government born amid deep polarization: for some, it represents the promise of economic stability; for others, the return of a political project that rubs salt into wounds that never fully healed. Fujimori received the presidential sash amid applause after taking the oath of office and vowed to lead a “safe, prosperous, and united” country.

results.title: Keiko Fujimori
highlights:
Keiko Sofía Fujimori Higuchi (born 25 May 1975) is a Peruvian politician who has served as the president of Peru since 2026. The eldest daughter of former president Alberto Fujimori, she is the leading figure of Fujimorism, the conservative political movement associated with her father, and has led its party, Popular Force, since 2010. Fujimori served as First Lady of Peru from 1994 to 2000 and as a member of Congress for Lima from 2006 to 2011. After advancing to the runoff but losing in the 2011, 2016, and 2021 presidential elections, she won the presidency on her fourth attempt in 2026. Fujimori is the first woman to be elected President of Peru.
...
Fujimori ran for president in four consecutive general elections (2011, 2016, 2021 and 2026) and is the only candidate in modern Peruvian history to reach four consecutive presidential runoffs. She lost the first three by narrow margins before defeating Roberto Sánchez in 2026, becoming the first woman elected president of Peru and returning Fujimorism to power 25 years after her father's government collapsed. Her platforms consistently combined hardline security policies with defense of Peru's market-oriented economic model, while her handling of her father's legacy shifted from distance to open embrace.
...
Fujimori was inaugurated on 28 July 2026 in Lima. She became Peru's 10th president since 2016 and the country’s first female elected president. Following her inauguration, she vowed to strengthened ties between Peru and the United States.
